Your converted model uses the text encoder and VAE from your checkpoint. SDXL includes both text encoders.

SD1.5: 512 × 512, Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 target. SDXL: 1024 × 1024, Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 target. Full SDXL conversion worked in the reported WAI Illustrious v170 phone test. Full SD1.5 component conversion still needs phone validation.
Converts SD1.5 and SDXL image models to run on your phone’s Qualcomm AI processor.
The app includes a prepared model structure. Your phone fills it with your model’s weights and builds the final file.
• QAIRT 2.50; SDXL UNet uses INT8 weights and 16-bit activations
• Both families convert their own text encoders and VAE encoder/decoder
SD1.5 converts the checkpoint UNet, text encoder, and VAE encoder and decoder on your phone.
SDXL converts the checkpoint UNet, both text encoders (CLIP-L and CLIP-G), and the VAE encoder and decoder on your phone.
The checkpoint must contain all required components. Missing or incompatible tensors stop conversion; another model’s weights are not substituted. The standard tokenizer is reused.

Earlier UNet conversions worked for CyberRealistic, DreamShaper 8 and AbsoluteReality. MistoonAnime produced noise when using shared CLIP and VAE files; checkpoint-owned components have not yet been tested for that model.

Replacing only Pony’s text encoders fixed the tested Pony model. The user also reports excellent output after full checkpoint-owned conversion of WAI Illustrious v170. Other checkpoints remain unverified; the UNet still uses fixed calibrated activation ranges.
UNet adapter weights are merged during conversion, with no extra work at generation time. Several adapters can be combined.
Supported: standard kohya UNet LoRAs (lora_down / lora_up / alpha).
Not supported: diffusers/PEFT format, LoCon, LyCORIS, LoHa, DoRA, IA3. These fail with a clear message rather than producing a bad model.
Only attention modules have been tested; convolution adapters should work but are unverified.
Text-encoder LoRA weights are not merged. Adapters containing only text-encoder weights are unsupported.
Strength is baked in, not a slider you can move later: two strengths of one adapter are two separate models.
What it needs from your phone
• Earlier SD1.5 conversion measured about 4.8 GB of RAM at peak
• Earlier UNet-only SD1.5 conversion needed about 4 GB of working storage; full component conversion needs additional space
• Earlier exports were about 1.3 GB for SD1.5 and 3.5 GB for SDXL; checkpoint-owned components can change the size
• The earlier SDXL UNet conversion took 7 minutes 17 seconds; converting CLIP and VAE adds work
• SDXL uses temporary files to reduce RAM use, so it needs extra free storage
• Peak SDXL phone RAM has not been measured
How to tell what went wrong
Noise can involve incompatible weights, template activation ranges or generation settings. Check the conversion log before drawing conclusions.
Model loading depends on the target chip and the QNN runtime in your generator.
Older SDXL exports used shared CLIP weights, which broke the tested Pony model. Reconvert to include its own text encoders.
Colour or detail problems need investigation; appearance alone does not identify the cause.

Earlier SD1.5 and SDXL UNet conversions worked on a Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra. The user now confirms full SDXL component conversion and good output for WAI Illustrious v170. Full SD1.5 component conversion remains unverified on a phone.
The reported WAI Illustrious v170 result used NPU, 1024 × 1024, 30 steps, CFG 7 and seed 418928922; generation took 45.8 seconds. This is one reported run, not a cross-device benchmark.
The UNet, text encoder and VAE are converted from this checkpoint. SDXL includes both text encoders. No shared model download is needed.
